It is known that some complexity increase is always guaranteed, as shown in [2]. The amount of this increase may depend on x. If x is a random codeword of an error-correcting code, then the changed version of x contains all the information both about x itself and the places where it was changed. This leads to the maximal increase in complexity. The minimal increase, as shown in [2], happens for x that is a random element of the Hamming ball of some radius with center 0n . However, the natural question: which functions may appear as d 7→ (the maximal complexity of strings in the d-ball centered at x), remains open. In our paper we study the typical complexity of a string that can be obtained from x by changing a fraction of bits chosen randomly.
